newsitem.title: ALGERIA: Algerians hail pipeline as triumph over odds.
newsitem.headline: Algerians hail pipeline as triumph over odds.

text.p: When officials inaugurated Algeria's Maghreb pipeline at the weekend, running 1,385 km (865 miles) to Spain, they achieved a dream that should turn rapidly into hard cash and seal economic ties across the Mediterranean.

"It was a dream becoming true. Few people believed in this project 25 months ago," Algerian Energy Minister Amar Makhloufi told foreign guests and reporters shortly after the $2.3 billion gas pipeline went officially on stream on Saturday.

Early on Sunday, the first gas sent through one of the four gates at Hassi-R'mel Gas Dispatching National Centre at the inauguration ceremony reached the Moroccan border after a 15-hour journey across more than 500 km (300 miles).

From there the gas through the pipeline -- initial annual capacity 9.5 billion cubic metres (335 billion cubic feet) -- crosses Morocco to near the northern city of Tangiers, under the Strait of Gibraltar, and on to the Spanish city of Cordoba and a link with Portugal's gas network.

"It was a real challenge. The work streched over an area none had visited before. There were no means to (parts of) the area. There were only the stars," recalled Hadjadj Mohamed, project head, speaking in the shade of a bedouin tent set up for guests flown from Algiers, Morocco, Spain and Portugal.

"Without doubt, the new pipeline is one among the great and ambitious projects achieved in the past years. It will be the main vehicle in developing relations between the Maghreb and Europe," said Spain's Industry and Energy Minister Josep Pique.
Scores of men, armed with traditional shotguns and drums, fired into the air and beat on drums in celebration yards from the sophisticated complex.

According to officials, in 1995 a quarter of the European Union natural gas imports were from Algeria's seven gas fields. Hassi-R'Mel produced 90.51 billion cubic metres (3.196 trillion cubic feet) last year from overall gas output of 114.7 billion cubic metres (4.051 trillion cubic feet), they said.
Algerian officials told Reuters they forecast Hassi-R'Mel would produce 94.2 billion cubic metres (3.327 trillion cubic feet) this year.
They said that more than 2.18 million tonnes of crude oil also came from Hassi-R'Mel in 1995 out of Algeria's total 35.37 million tonnes of crude from 11 oilfields.
Hassi Messaoud, southeast of Hassi-R'Mel, dominated the North African OPEC member's oil production with 19.74 million tonnes last year.
Hadjadj took part in 1980 in building the first pipeline, known as Transmed, carrying 24 billion cubic metres (848 billion cubic feet) of gas from Hassi-R'Mel to Italy through neighbouring Tunisia.
He termed the latest project "a successful adventure of 3,000 men and state-of-the art technology and management".

"One of the main difficulties was how to gather equipement and get it quickly to the site and how to coordinate more than 20 partners involved in the work and get them moving at the right time and the right place," he said.
He and other technicians said advanced technology helped the 500 foreigners and 2,500 Algerian workers overcome natural odds.
They said a huge digger allowed them to cut up to three km (two miles) of canals a day and saved them from the headache of using explosives.

"It needs time to get authorisations for using explosives and a mobilisation of soldiers and security forces to protect its transport," said Hadjadj, referring to possible attacks by Moslem guerrillas seeking explosives to use for bombs.
